Subject: Initial onboarding — network constraints & egress requirements

- IP allowlist and required outbound FQDNs for control plane and model fetch
- Firewall rules (ports, protocols) and whether SNI-based allowlisting is sufficient

Hi Priya — thanks for the context and the constraints doc. Attached is a short checklist for private deployments that covers the usual allowlist, firewall and proxy patterns. Summary below; full checklist attached.

Key items (minimal required for private endpoints):

1) Control plane & runtime egress endpoints (DNS and short notes):
   - control.redwood-inference.net (TLS 443) — management calls, configuration sync, heartbeats
   - models.redwood-inference.net (TLS 443) — on-demand model fetch and updates
   - metrics.ingest.redwood-inference.net (TLS 443) — telemetry (can be disabled if required)

   Note: We recommend allowing the above FQDNs and outbound 443 to the resolved IP ranges. If you cannot allow FQDN-based egress, we'll provide a scoped CIDR list per-region on request.

2) Firewall rules (customer-facing):
   - Outbound 443 to the FQDNs above.
   - Allow DNS (UDP/TCP 53) to your resolver or an allowed DNS forwarder; recommend DoT/DoH if you enforce DNS privacy.
   - If you run a NAT gateway, ensure ephemeral ports (>=1024) are allowed for return flows.

3) TLS interception / proxy guidance:
   - We support customers using an outbound HTTPS proxy. However, we require transparent SNI passthrough or an ability to pin Redwood's certificate bundle when the proxy terminates TLS.
   - If your proxy performs TLS interception with custom CA, provide the proxy CA cert so we can advise on mTLS/connector cert interactions; some client flows use mTLS and won't function through a MITM.

4) mTLS & certificate expectations:
   - For control-plane webhooks and admin RPCs we use mutual TLS for high-trust configs. Keystone SANs: CN=control.redwood-inference.net, SANs include control.redwood-inference.net and control.us.redwood-inference.net.

5) Audit & evidence items we can provide:
   - Signed certificate chain samples (PEM), expected SNI hostnames, sample TLS fingerprints, recommended firewall rule text, connectivity test script.

Attachments: redwood-private-network-checklist.pdf (contains per-region CIDR export and sample iptables/ACL entries).

If you'd like, we can provide a short connectivity-testing script and a temporary IP/CIDR snapshot for your firewall team to validate prior to cutover.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Security Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood-private-network-checklist.pdf]

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com

Neha — quick operations notes to add to the checklist before we hand this to Boreal's net team:

- NAT & ephemeral port guidance: if Boreal uses source-NAT with many connectors behind one public IP, document that we see X-Forwarded-For for observability. Recommend mapping persistent connector IDs to distinct IPs where possible for easier auditing.
- DNS ownership model: prefer customer-managed resolver + conditional forwarder to a trusted DNS egress point. If Boreal cannot allow external DNS, we can accept an allowlist of IPs resolved at time-of-onboarding and a weekly rotation window for updates.
- SNI-based allowlisting caveat: SNI is effective for host-level filtering but not for HTTP/2 multiplexed flows or encrypted SNI (ESNI). Where customers use TLS interception + ESNI, we'll need a proxy exception or certificate pinning strategy.
- If Boreal requires zero outbound to cloud, propose a pull model using signed artifacts delivered via air-gapped media; this requires offline model delivery and is a longer path.

I'll add two sample firewall rule snippets to the checklist file and drop a per-region CIDR snapshot.

— Jonas
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Sameer — thanks for the details and the inventory. Short answers and next steps below.

Short answers:
- Proxy with internal CA: Supported but with caveats. Our recommended approach is one of the following (ranked by fidelity):
  1) Allow SNI passthrough to control.redwood-inference.net and models.redwood-inference.net (no TLS interception). Simplest and fully supported.
  2) If interception is mandatory, install the corporate proxy CA in the connector host trust store and provide us a copy of the proxy CA chain so we can validate mTLS handshake compatibility. Note: some mTLS flows will fail if the proxy rewrites client certs.
  3) Use a customer-managed outbound NAT with a dedicated public IP range and request a time-limited CIDR snapshot from Redwood for test windows; we'll provide a one-week test CIDR list scoped to your account.

- Time-limited CIDR snapshot: We'll generate a per-account CIDR list for a 7-day test window and share a signed manifest. Plan: our infra team will send the snapshot within 24 hours after you confirm the test window start.

Mutual action plan (MAP):
1) Confirm test window start (Boreal) — target: Mon 19 Jan 2026
2) Redwood provides 7-day CIDR snapshot + connectivity test script (Neha/Jonas) — by Mon 19 Jan 2026 09:00 PST
3) Boreal firewall team applies rules in a maintenance window and runs tests; share results + pcap if failures (Sameer) — by Tue 20 Jan 2026 EOD
4) If TLS-intercept issues are detected, iterate on proxy CA install or request dedicated NAT (decide by Wed 21 Jan 2026)
5) Post-validation: sign off and move to production cutover planning.

Attachments included in this thread: redwood-private-network-checklist.pdf, boreal-egress-reqs.xlsx, boreal-network-constraints.docx.

If that MAP looks good, reply with your preferred test start time and I'll kick off the CIDR snapshot generation.

Best regards,
Neha Kapoor
Security Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
